entrypoints.summary: A gossip-cluster peer can supply a crafted member name; an operator later requests the Alertmanager HTTP status page at /multitenant_alertmanager/status.

affected_components.role: Vulnerable HTML status-template construction and rendering of gossip cluster member fields.
Same template-package pattern updated as defense in depth.

causal_paths.kind: gossip member name to HTML status response

observability.channel: operator browser rendering of the HTTP status page
negative_controls: A fixed handler escapes HTML-special characters in peer names.
The response document does not retain a browser-interpretable raw script tag from the injected member name.
observability.positive_marker: Injected member-name markup is executed as JavaScript rather than displayed as escaped text.

preconditions: The actor has network access to the Alertmanager gossip cluster.
An operator visits /multitenant_alertmanager/status after the crafted member metadata is present.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: A gossip member name such as <script>alert(document.cookie)</script>.
trigger_steps.summary: Join or advertise to the gossip cluster using a member name containing script markup.
Cause an operator to open the Alertmanager status page, which renders the stored member entry.

capabilities.concept: inject markup through gossip member metadata
execute script in an operator status-page browser

impacts.concept: operator session or Alertmanager API action compromise

relation_candidates.dst: inject markup through gossip member metadata
relation_candidates.rationale: The report states that a node with network access can join the gossip cluster with a crafted name.

relation_candidates.dst: execute script in an operator status-page browser
relation_candidates.rationale: The text/template status renderer inserts the crafted member name into HTML without automatic escaping, and the report describes browser JavaScript execution when the operator visits the page.
relation_candidates.src: inject markup through gossip member metadata

relation_candidates.dst: operator session or Alertmanager API action compromise
relation_candidates.rationale: The audit identifies session hijacking, credential theft, and unauthorized Alertmanager API actions as potential consequences of arbitrary JavaScript execution.
relation_candidates.src: execute script in an operator status-page browser

relation_candidates.rationale: The project replaced text/template with html/template, whose automatic HTML escaping prevents injected markup from being interpreted as script.
relation_candidates.src: execute script in an operator status-page browser

impact.affected_asset: Operator browser session and the operator's authenticated access to Alertmanager.
impact.attacker_capability: Execute arbitrary JavaScript in the browser of an operator who visits the status page; the audit identifies potential session hijacking, credential theft, and unauthorized Alertmanager API actions.
impact.security_effect: Stored cross-site scripting in the Alertmanager status page

causal_trace.summary: An actor with network access to the gossip cluster joins as a peer using a crafted member name containing HTML/JavaScript markup.
The status page treats gossip-derived member Name and Addr data as safe for an HTML document, although these values require HTML-context encoding before rendering.
pkg/alertmanager/alertmanager_http.go parses the status template with Go text/template and interpolates member fields into HTML; text/template does not automatically escape HTML.
When an operator visits the status page, the crafted peer name is interpreted as executable JavaScript in the operator browser rather than displayed as text.

failure.operation: Rendering gossip member fields through text/template into the Alertmanager HTML status response

primary_invariant.statement: Gossip-derived member fields rendered in an HTML status page must be contextually HTML-escaped before browser interpretation.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The handler used text/template, whose interpolation of Name and Addr into HTML does not auto-escape special characters.

quality.review_notes: The audit supplies a concrete gossip-member-name proof of concept, template excerpt, and browser-execution outcome. The reviewed PR states that TestStatusHandler_HTMLEscaping was added, but the available material contains no test-run result and no full assertion body; therefore this record treats the test as an oracle contract, not observed execution. The Store Gateway change is documented as defense in depth and is not asserted here as a presently exploitable path.

remediation.invariant_restored: Both status handlers use html/template so HTML-special characters in rendered values are escaped rather than interpreted as markup.

affected_versions_or_commits.value: Versions/commits before the PR #7512 merge commit af9c40c on 2026-05-12

target.component: Alertmanager gossip-cluster status page; related Store Gateway status handler

oracle.expected_negative: The raw markup must not remain browser-interpretable in the rendered output; the response document should not include unescaped injected script markup.
oracle.expected_positive: A peer or tenant value containing HTML-special characters or an XSS payload is rendered in escaped form.
